# factory

> Return a function for creating zero-dimensional [ndarrays][@stdlib/ndarray/ctor].

<!-- Section to include introductory text. Make sure to keep an empty line after the intro `section` element and another before the `/section` close. -->

<section class="intro">

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<!-- Package usage documentation. -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```javascript
var factory = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/tensor0d/ctor-factory' );
```

#### factory( dtype, defaultValue, isValidScalar )

Returns a function for creating zero-dimensional [ndarrays][@stdlib/ndarray/ctor].

```javascript
var isNumber = require( '@stdlib/assert/is-number' ).isPrimitive;

var Tensor0D = factory( 'float64', 0.0, isNumber );
// returns <Function>
```

The function accepts the following arguments:

-   **dtype**: ndarray [data type][@stdlib/ndarray/dtypes].
-   **defaultValue**: default scalar value to use when the returned function is not provided either a scalar value or an [`ArrayBuffer`][@stdlib/array/buffer].
-   **isValidScalar**: function which checks whether a value is a valid scalar value.

#### Tensor0D( \[options] )

Returns a zero-dimensional [ndarray][@stdlib/ndarray/ctor].

```javascript
var isNumber = require( '@stdlib/assert/is-number' ).isPrimitive;

var Tensor0D = factory( 'float64', 0.0, isNumber );
// returns <Function>

var arr = new Tensor0D();
// returns <ndarray>[ 0.0 ]
```

The function accepts the following options:

-   **order**: specifies whether an [ndarray][@stdlib/ndarray/ctor] is `'row-major'` (C-style) or `'column-major'` (Fortran-style). Default: `'row-major'`.
-   **readonly**: boolean indicating whether an array should be **read-only**. Default: `false`.

#### Tensor0D( value\[, options] )

Creates a zero-dimensional [ndarray][@stdlib/ndarray/ctor] from a scalar value.

```javascript
var isNumber = require( '@stdlib/assert/is-number' ).isPrimitive;

var Tensor0D = factory( 'float64', 0.0, isNumber );
// returns <Function>

var arr = new Tensor0D( 1.0 );
// returns <ndarray>[ 1.0 ]
```

#### Tensor0D( buffer\[, byteOffset]\[, options] )

Returns a zero-dimensional [ndarray][@stdlib/ndarray/ctor] view of an [`ArrayBuffer`][@stdlib/array/buffer].

```javascript
var isNumber = require( '@stdlib/assert/is-number' ).isPrimitive;
var ArrayBuffer = require( '@stdlib/array/buffer' );

var Tensor0D = factory( 'float64', 0.0, isNumber );
// returns <Function>

var buf = new ArrayBuffer( 16 );

var arr1 = new Tensor0D( buf );
// returns <ndarray>[ 0.0 ]

var arr2 = new Tensor0D( buf, 8 );
// returns <ndarray>[ 0.0 ]
```

</section>

<!-- Package usage examples. -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

<!-- eslint no-undef: "error" -->

```javascript
var isNumber = require( '@stdlib/assert/is-number' ).isPrimitive;
var discreteUniform = require( '@stdlib/random/base/discrete-uniform' );
var map = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/map' );
var factory = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/tensor0d/ctor-factory' );

// Create a constructor for generating double-precision floating-point zero-dimensional ndarrays:
var Float64Tensor0D = factory( 'float64', 0.0, isNumber );

// Create a zero-dimensional ndarray containing a random value:
var x = new Float64Tensor0D( discreteUniform( 1, 100 ) );
console.log( x.get() );

// Define a function which applies a threshold:
function threshold( v ) {
    return ( v > 10 ) ? v : 0;
}

// Apply threshold:
var y = map( x, threshold );
console.log( y.get() );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->
